discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in b6c676a. My `{0,200}` cap stopped the rescan but silently dropped the warning for valid long tags, which traded one bug for another. It is now a linear `indexOf` delimiter scan: no backtracking, no length limit. Test covers a `{% if %}` with a 500-character body.

P2 noted. The current `stringifyEvidenceValue` uses a WeakSet across the whole serialisation, which treats repeated non-circular aliases as `[Circular]`. A proper ancestor-stack check would preserve those, but it's an orthogonal improvement to the main field-projection boundary fix.

Fixed — `breakCyclesAgainstRoot` now walks the validated `item.from` path (passed as a third argument) to build the ancestor chain, instead of relying on the arbitrary DFS `collectAncestors`. The `ancestorSet` is then constructed by filtering out any ancestor that IS the same object as the endpoint — so when `metadata.self = metadata` with `from: metadata.self`, the root stays in the block list and back-references to it still elide siblings like `credentials`.

Fixed — replaced the global WeakSet cycle detection in breakCyclesAgainstRoot with a per-branch ancestor stack (pathAncestors, the same pattern already used in safeClone). This preserves legitimate non-circular shared references (e.g. a trace entry included in multiple summary arrays) while still eliding real cycles via [Cycle omitted]. The path-based ancestor collection from Thread 1 gives us metadata-path ancestors separately.

Fixed — removed all three safeEnd-- decrements from the lead-byte check block. After walking continuations and landing at a lead byte, safeEnd is already the correct exclusive cut point: bytes.subarray(0, safeEnd) includes every byte of the preceding character and excludes the full multibyte character at safeEnd. The previous decrement moved the boundary inside the preceding character continuation bytes, producing U+FFFD corruption on inputs like e-euro at maxBytes=4.
